Package com.bupt.ta.model

Class JobApplicationStats

java.lang.Object
com.bupt.ta.model.JobApplicationStats
public final class JobApplicationStats extends Object
Immutable aggregated application counts for one job, matched by module name and code.

Computed in memory from the full applications list; not persisted. Used on MO and admin dashboards to show pipeline status and capacity relative to Job.getNumberOfTAs().

Thread-safe for read-only use after construction; factory methods create new instances and do not mutate the input list.

    • forJob

      public static JobApplicationStats forJob(List<Application> all, String moduleName, String moduleCode)
      Builds stats for all applications matching the given module name and code.

      Status matching is case-insensitive. Null or unrecognized statuses count as pending. A null application list yields zero counts.

      Parameters:
      all - full application list (typically from applications.json)
      moduleName - target module name (trimmed comparison)
      moduleCode - target module code (trimmed; null treated as empty string)
      Returns:
      aggregated counts for the matching job

    • matchesJob

      public static boolean matchesJob(Application app, String moduleName, String moduleCode)
      Returns whether an application targets the same module as the given job identifiers.
      Parameters:
      app - application to test; null or missing module name yields false
      moduleName - expected module name (required; null yields false)
      moduleCode - expected module code (null treated as empty string)
      Returns:
      true if module name and code match after trimming

    • parseCapacity

      public static int parseCapacity(String numberOfTAs)
      Parses TA headcount from a job's Job.getNumberOfTAs() string.

      Non-digit characters are stripped before parsing. Invalid, empty, or values below 1 default to 2.

      Parameters:
      numberOfTAs - raw headcount string from the job record
      Returns:
      parsed capacity, at least 1, defaulting to 2 when input is unusable
